title.narrative: Girls’ Inequality Reduction for Living in Safer Online Space without Fear: GIRLS without Fear

description.narrative:
01: Strengthened capacities and engagement opportunities of central and local duty-bearers (MoE, MSDHS, MDES and provincial branches) and right-holder representatives (CSOs, children and Youth Councils,) to jointly design gender responsive, age-appropriate online safely and digital literacy curriculums • Establishment of Provincial Working Groups in 5 selected provinces in Thailand to oversee and support Action activities for developing and piloting curriculum packages, including awareness seminars about online safety; • Sign tripartite MoU for collaboration and cooperation with MoE, MSDHS, MDES;
02: Strengthened capacities of MoE teachers and Thai Children and Youth Council members to teach online safety and digital literacy in 5 targeted provinces. • Development of national hybrid e-learning and face to face curriculum platform customized for parents, teachers and students that enables children and youth (CAYs) to utilize internet and social media positively for their full development; • Through participatory approach involving students (particularly girls and young women), teachers and parents, pilot curriculums in schools to learn, refine and test to build solid evidence base for MoE, and MSDHS’s Thailand Children and Youth Councils to adopt standard curriculum packages; • 15 Trainings of Trainers (ToTs) (Face to face) of public school teachers in 5 target provinces in Thailand for piloting online safety and digital 1 literacy curriculum including gender transformative approach and guidance on how to interview students about internet use or abuse, use digital technology safely and positively coupled with fun learning activities. Successive rounds of ToT’s build on previous ones based on refinements and reflections from piloted curriculum material; • 15 ToTs (Face to face) of Thailand Children and Youth Council members in 5 target provinces in Thailand for piloting online safety and digital literacy curriculum including gender transformative approach, safe Intemet and human-rights based approach. Successive rounds of ToT’s build on previous ones based on refinements and reflections from piloted curriculum material; • MoE & MSDHS curriculum integration planning and budgeting. 03: Strengthened capacities and opportunities ofgirls and boys andfemale

Plan International (“Plan”) has been working to advance children’s rights and empower girls in Asia for 74 years, and in Thailand for 41 years. Internet Foundation for Development of Thailand (“IFDT”) is a locally registered foundation established in Thailand working to educate rights holders and duty bearers about safe internet use for children and young persons for over 20 years. Both applicants have extensive experience working with online child and youth protection in close collaboration with civil society networks, government authorities in Thailand as well as ASEAN children and youth forums. This Action has emerged from research and consultations with children, youth, and civil society groups that have a common vision of online safety for Thailand’s new generation and utilizing the vast potential of the internet for their positive development and knowledge. Plan and IFDT worked with the CRC Thailand in drafting Universal Periodic Review (UPR) recommendations for the Royal Thai Government (RTG) which featured online safety as its priority concern. In 2023, the Thailand Safe Internet Coalition (TSIC), together with IFDT, successfully persuaded the RTG cabinet to establish the annual “Internet Safer Day” which will be celebrated for the first time in Thailand in 2024. IFDT has also succeeded in proposing amendments to the criminal law to cover new online threats such as child online grooming, sexting, sextortion, cyber stalking and cyber bullying. It has been approved in principle by the Thai cabinet. IFDT is now working with the Ministry of Justice to implement a step-by-step amendment to the law. Though these developments have been quite positive, there remains a huge gap in bringing comprehensive awareness of internet safety issues and digital literacy to Thailand’s children and youth at the scale necessary to protect from being harmed through online abuse. To date, despite efforts from many CSOs, children and youth in all of their diversity, the Ministry of Education does not yet have a standardized curriculum and approach to face these rapidly evolving online challenges, leaving Thailand’s youth vulnerable without the skills to protect themselves online and digital literacy to navigate the virtual world.

SUMMARY: The overall objective is to promote the fulfilment of Thai children and youth’s digital rights in inclusive, safe and gender/age-responsive online spaces in line with the UN Child Rights Convention. The specific objective is to facilitate strengthened systems and frameworks which promote safe and equitable engagement of Thai children and youth in online spaces, in 5 provinces in Thailand. This ambition brings together children and youth, civil society, government authorities and the private sector to address a common goal that impacts society and the future of Thailand’s new generation. It supports Thailand’s governance and development process, respecting human rights and democratic principles, with a view to the achievement of the sustainable development goals (SDGs). In order to achieve these objectives, the Action brings together diverse stakeholders to develop a dynamic, participatory approach enabling children and youth to thrive in a rapidly changing virtual environment.

The Action capitalizes on a strongly-expressed and urgent need in Thailand to protect children and youth in all of their diversity from online threats and abuse while increasing their digital literacy and resilience when accessing the internet and social media. To achieve this, we propose a mutually-reinforcing intervention logic. The supporting outcomes lay the foundations of the specific and ultimately the overall objective through facilitating the implementation of a gender-responsive and age-appropriate national curriculum for online safety (01+2), empowering children and youth to claim their rights safely and positively (03), and ensuring duty bearers possess knowledge, take action and are accountable for actions needed to actualise a safe online environment that supports the protection of Thailand’s children and youth from all backgrounds and intersectional vulnerabilities (04). While 01, 02 and 03 are focused on strengthening rights holders’ capacities to know about, claim and enjoy their rights, 01 and 03 are focused on addressing capacity caps of duty bearers in terms of respecting, protecting and realising the rights of children, and on reinforcing their transparency and accountability. Activities under 01 and 02 focus on bringing together key and diverse stakeholders, developing and piloting a hybrid curriculum, and facilitating the adoption of this curriculum nationwide. Activities under 03 focus on peer education, youth-designed and -led advocacy action, meaningful child and youth engagement with duty bearers, and public awareness raising. Activities under 04 focus on engaging duty bearers at all levels (from caregivers, to law enforcement, to local/national governance), facilitating implementation and socialisation of existing legislation, and working with private sector stakeholders towards child protection aims. To mitigate the safeguarding risks of children and young people, the action will strictly observe protection and safeguarding protocols and the “Do no harm” principle in all levels of child and youth engagement. The risk of limited participation of rights holders and/or duty bearers will be mitigated through their meaningful inciusion in the design, implementation and management of the Action. We assume that all stakeholders will be willing and able to participate to the extent indicated in prior consultations

The Action directly targets both rights holders and duty bearers in Thailand, including 30,000 children, 600 children and youth council members, 600 teachers, 1,500 parents/caregivers, 1,600 duty bearers (social workers, law enforcement), 5 private sector/tech companies, 42 CRC Thailand member organisations, and representatives from key government ministries. Rights holders will be supported to better understand their protection rights and risk behaviours and will become empowered to claim those rights and to act in support of online safety. Duty bearers will work with rights holders to contribute towards preventing and responding to online risks for children, in support of a protective and enabling environment in Thailand that is in line with the government's commitments to online safety and child protection

technical Level: The project focuses on capacity-building through tailored curricula for children, caregivers, and duty bearers. These materials equip participants with knowledge and skills to prevent and respond to online safety risks. Girls, in particular, gain agency and leadership skills to advocate for safer digital environments. Caregivers and institutions (e.g. schools, social workers, government, private sector) are trained to create a stronger protective ecosystem. Collaboration is strengthened through existing and new structures, supported by intergenerational and intersectional dialogue.
Economic Level: Youth camps and Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) activities provide children and youth with practical skills in fundraising, advocacy, ICT, and financial management. These capabilities help them access government funding in the short term and improve future employment prospects.
Social Level: The Action fosters a safe and inclusive environment by promoting collaboration among civil society, public and private actors. Intergenerational dialogue ensures diverse voices are heard. By empowering youth—especially girls—to lead advocacy, the project enhances resilience, rights awareness, and long-term social change through a gender-transformative approach.
Policy Level: The project advocates for institutional adoption of the curricula by the Ministry of Education and the Department of Children and Youth. Youth-led advocacy also targets national and regional policy improvements on online safety, including legal reforms and ASEAN-level engagement.
